recipes.title: Jerk Chicken (Oven/Grill-Pan)
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of dark, glazed jerk chicken with rice and peas and coleslaw
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Jerk Chicken on a Traditional Drum Grill
recipes.prep_alt: Jerk chicken pieces cooking in a wire basket over a smoking oil-drum jerk pit

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a food processor or blender, combine the scallion, garlic, scotch bonnet, allspice, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg, brown sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, oil, and salt. Blend to a coarse, spoonable paste (add a splash of water if it won't move).
Pat the chicken thighs dry and score the skin a few times. Rub the jerk paste all over, working some under the skin where you can reach.
Marinate at least 1 hour in the fridge - overnight develops noticeably more flavor if you have the time.
Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Arrange the chicken skin-side up on a lined baking sheet or rack.
Bake 40-45 minutes, until the internal temperature reads 165°F (74°C) and the edges look deeply charred.
For extra char, finish 2-3 minutes under the broiler, or sear skin-side down in a hot grill pan for 2-3 minutes before baking.
Rest 5 minutes, then serve with rice and peas or festival (fried dumplings), with extra scotch bonnet on the side for anyone who wants more heat.

recipes.title: Curry Chicken (Jamaican-Style)
recipes.dish_alt: Yellow curry chicken pieces with bell peppers served beside rice
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Jamaican-Style Curry With Rice and Peas
recipes.prep_alt: A Jamaican curry (curry goat) simmered in gravy and served over rice and peas

sections.heading: Steps
items: Toss the chicken with half the curry powder, the all-purpose seasoning, ginger, and a pinch of black pepper. Cover and marinate at least 1 hour - overnight is better.

Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the remaining curry powder and "burn" it - stir constantly for 30-45 seconds until fragrant and a shade darker, watching closely so it doesn't scorch.
Add the marinated chicken and sear 4-5 minutes per side until browned and well coated in the curry.
Add the onion, garlic, and scallion, stirring 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add the potato, the whole scotch bonnet (if using), and the stock or water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender, the potato is cooked through, and the sauce has thickened. Remove the whole scotch bonnet before serving.
Season with salt to taste. Serve hot over rice.

recipes.title: Ackee and Saltfish
recipes.dish_alt: Flaked saltfish gently folded with pale yellow ackee, scallion, and tomato
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Ackee and Saltfish on a Breakfast Platter
recipes.prep_alt: Ackee and saltfish served as part of a full Jamaican breakfast platter with callaloo and johnny cake

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Scotch bonnet pepper, minced to taste
Salt, to taste (go easy — the fish is already salty)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Soak the saltfish in cold water at least 8 hours (or overnight), changing the water once or twice, to pull out the excess salt.
Drain, then simmer the saltfish in fresh water 10-15 minutes until tender. Drain again, cool slightly, and flake into bite-size pieces, discarding any skin or bones.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, scallion, thyme, and scotch bonnet, cooking 5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomato and bell pepper, cooking 3-4 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
Stir in the flaked saltfish and sauté 2-3 minutes.
Gently fold in the ackee - it's delicate and already cooked (canned), so stir softly to avoid mashing it. Cook 4-5 minutes just to heat through.
Season with black pepper, going easy on salt since the fish is already salty. Serve hot with fried dumplings or, for a full dinner plate, rice and peas and fried plantain.

recipes.title: Oxtail Stew with Butter Beans
recipes.dish_alt: Deeply browned oxtail pieces in a thick gravy with butter beans
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Jamaican Stew Peas, a Close Cousin
recipes.prep_alt: Jamaican stew peas, a related braised-meat-and-beans dish, served over rice

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the oxtail dry and season with salt, pepper, thyme, allspice, and the browning sauce. Marinate at least 30 minutes - overnight is better.
Heat oil in a heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the oxtail in batches, 2-3 minutes per side, until well browned. Remove to a plate.
In the same pot, add the onion and cook 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, ginger, and scallion, cooking 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Return the oxtail to the pot along with the Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, the whole scotch bonnet, and the beef stock or water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer on low 2-2.5 hours (or pressure cook about 45 minutes), until the oxtail is fork-tender, adding a splash more liquid if it reduces too much.
Add the carrot and butter beans, then simmer uncovered 20-30 minutes more, until the carrot is tender and the sauce has thickened into a gravy. Remove the whole scotch bonnet.
Season with salt to taste. Serve hot over rice and peas.

recipes.title: Escovitch Fish
recipes.dish_alt: Whole fried fish topped generously with pickled carrot, onion, and pepper strips
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Escovitch Fish Plated With Festival
recipes.prep_alt: Fried escovitch fish served in a takeout box with festival, rice, cabbage, and plantain

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Fish fillets (snapper or firm white fish)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the fish with salt, pepper, and lime juice. Let sit 10 minutes.
Dredge the fish lightly in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the fish 3-4 minutes per side until golden, crisp, and cooked through. Remove to a plate lined with paper towel.

Pour off all but about a tablespoon of oil from the skillet. Add the carrot, onion, bell pepper, scotch bonnet, and allspice berries, and sauté 2-3 minutes until just softened but still with some bite.
Add the vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer and cook 3-4 minutes.
Spoon the hot pickled vegetables and their liquid generously over the fried fish.
It's best served after resting 20-30 minutes (or even overnight) so the fish soaks up the pickle - but it's good hot too if you're hungry now. Serve with festival or bammy.

recipes.title: Brown Stew Chicken
recipes.dish_alt: Chicken pieces in a rich brown gravy with rice and peas
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Brown Stew Chicken Alongside Jerk Chicken
recipes.prep_alt: A plate of brown stew chicken with fries next to a plate of grilled jerk chicken

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the chicken with salt, pepper, garlic, thyme, allspice, and the browning sauce. Marinate 30 minutes to overnight.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces 3-4 minutes per side until deeply colored. Remove to a plate.
In the same pot, add the onion, scallion, and bell pepper, cooking 3-4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the ketchup and cook 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the pot, add the carrot, the whole scotch bonnet, and the stock or water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened into a gravy.
Remove the whole scotch bonnet, season with salt to taste, and serve hot with rice and peas or steamed cabbage.

recipes.title: Jamaican Beef Patties (Dinner Plate)
recipes.dish_alt: A golden, curry-yellow Jamaican beef patty held in a paper wrapper
recipes.prep_alt: A Jamaican beef patty broken open showing the spiced ground beef filling inside the flaky crust

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the dough: whisk the flour, curry powder, turmeric, salt, and baking powder together. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs. Add ice water gradually, mixing just until it comes together into a dough. Wrap and chill at least 30 minutes.
Make the filling: heat a splash of oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic, scallion, thyme, scotch bonnet, and allspice 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up as it cooks, until browned, about 5-6 minutes.
Stir in the breadcrumbs, beef stock, and soy sauce, and simmer 2-3 minutes until moist but holding together, not soupy. Season with salt and pepper, then cool to room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the chilled dough thin and cut into circles about 12-14cm across.
Spoon the filling onto one half of each circle, fold over, and crimp the edge firmly with a fork to seal.
Brush with the egg wash and bake 25-30 minutes until deep golden and flaky.
Serve 2 patties per person as a full dinner plate, with a simple side - steamed cabbage, coleslaw, or rice and peas - to round it out.

recipes.title: Jamaican Rum Cake (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: A boxed Buccaneer-brand Jamaican rum cake with a slice visible through the die-cut window
recipes.prep_alt: Boxed Tortuga-brand Jamaican rum fruit cake on a shop shelf

sections.heading: Steps
items: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C) and grease a small loaf pan, muffin tin, or mini bundt pan - scale the pan to your batch size.
Cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg(s) one at a time.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and nutmeg together in a separate bowl.
Alternate adding the dry ingredients and the coconut milk to the butter mixture, mixing just until combined. Stir in the rum and vanilla.
Pour into the prepared pan and bake 20-25 minutes for a muffin tin (35-40 minutes for a small loaf), until a toothpick comes out clean.
Meanwhile, make the glaze: combine the butter, sugar, and water in a small saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, then simmer 2-3 minutes until slightly syrupy. Off heat, stir in the rum.
While the cake is still warm, poke holes all over with a skewer and slowly spoon the warm glaze over, letting it soak in.
Cool at least 15 minutes before serving. It's even better the next day once the rum has fully soaked in, but perfectly good warm.
